S4.title: LangGraph 1.0 and 1.2 in 2026: Why Durable State Has Changed Everything for Python Agent Developers
S4.excerpt:
With version="v2", invoke() and stream() output are automatically coerced to declared Pydantic models — eliminating the manual parsing that was previously required and reducing a common source of type errors. Chat models now also expose a .profile attribute through model profiles (derived from models.dev), enabling the framework to automatically infer capabilities like structured output support and context limits.

## The 2026 Developer Landscape: LangGraph vs Everything Else [...] LangGraph 1.2 introduced type-safe streaming and invocation via a version="v2" parameter. Passing version="v2" to stream() or astream() now returns unified StreamPart output with type, ns, and data keys on every chunk — each with its own TypedDict, all importable from langgraph.types. For invoke(), version="v2" returns a GraphOutput object with .value and .interrupts attributes. bundles.summary:
I did not find a public, citable metric for **monthly active developers (MA-devs)** for the open-source **LangGraph (Python)** project specifically for **September 2026**. None of the provided sources reported an MA-devs time series or a September 2026 value.

Closest public proxy found (not MA-devs):
- **Monthly PyPI downloads / install activity**: One source claims LangGraph has “~34.5M / mo” monthly PyPI downloads in 2026, describing it as the “most-installed agent framework” (i.e., download/adoption activity rather than developer activity) [https://uvik.net/blog/langchain-vs-langgraph].

No public source evidence in the provided results specifies that this PyPI-download proxy is measured over the **September 2026** date range, nor does it define/approximate MA-devs.
